---
title: "Rust implementation and reuse"
---

## Architecture {#sec-implementation}

The numerical library is independent of the web page. Its FFT, initial-condition, growth, nLPT, sheet, and geometric-clipping modules originate in the MIT-licensed Hopf–Cole cosmology core. The source revision is recorded in [the decisions log](https://github.com/yipihey/precrossedsheet/blob/main/docs/decisions.md), and the original copyright is retained. The historical Rust crate name `hcc_core` is preserved for compatibility with the inherited tests and API links.

The new modules add cosmological PM evolution, initial-field and trajectory tangents, conservative sheet observables, and a checked laboratory request/response facade. The geometry visitor supplies the same periodic connectivity to Jacobian checks and continuous mode integration. This prevents a plotting mesh from silently differing from the sheet whose mass is measured.

| Layer | Responsibility | Reuse boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Grid and FFT | Periodic indexing, transforms, spectral operators | Standalone fields on 1D–3D grids |
| Growth and nLPT | Spatial recurrence and time factors | Fixed input modes, cosmology, perturbative order |
| Sheet and R3D | Conservative overlap integrals | Supplied unwrapped positions and optional P1 weights |
| Observables | Interval deposition, PDF measures, fixed-mass modes | Independent of how trajectories were generated |
| PM and tangents | Discrete cosmological evolution and JVPs | Supplied initial positions, momenta, directions |
| Laboratory facade | Validate inputs, report orientation, serialize reproducible results | Native Rust and Wasm use the same function |
| Browser worker | Own Wasm/GPU backends, serialize work and cancel obsolete requests | Shared trajectories and separately validated continuous observables |

## Build and inspect

Install Rust, the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target, wasm-pack, Python 3, and Quarto. From a checkout:

```sh
make test
make wasm
make api
make check
make site
python3 scripts/serve.py 8790 _site
```

`make test` runs native numerical and frontend contract tests. `make test-wasm` checks the generated binary in Node after `make wasm`; the browser self-check exercises its worker integration. `make wasm` writes the browser package into `app/pkg/`; `make api` publishes rustdoc into `api/`. The provenance checker resolves each equation's function link, each test badge, and each lab hash key. Quarto copies the standalone app, packaged data, and API documentation into the rendered book.

Open [the API reference](../api/hcc_core/index.html) for types, argument conventions, and implementation details. These pages are generated from the actual source used by the lab. A new project can depend on `core/` with a Cargo path dependency and use the same routines without Quarto or a browser.

```toml
[dependencies]
hcc-core = { path = "../precrossedsheet/core" }
```

```rust
use hcc_core::{Cosmo, ics::Preset};
let mut sim = Cosmo::new(2, 24, 1.0);
sim.keep_tensors = Some(true);
sim.set_ic_preset(Preset::PlaneWaves {
    modes: vec![([1, 0, 0], 0.3, 0.0), ([0, 1, 0], 0.2, 0.4)]
}, 0.0, 0.0);
sim.build_lpt(4);
let d = 0.4 * sim.shell_crossing(4);
assert!(sim.lpt_ref().min_jacobian(d, 4) > 0.0);
let density = sim.sheet_density_exact(d, 4, 32, false, 1e4);
```

For production use also check the affine simplex orientations and the resolution dependence. The high-level laboratory facade performs these checks automatically, but direct low-level callers remain responsible for input dimensions, field lengths, and validity.

## Numerical limits and derivative scope

The inherited LPT spatial fields and deposited density arrays use `f32`; Fourier arithmetic, clipping moments, PM state, and analytic tangent arithmetic use `f64`. A finite-difference check must choose its step above representation noise and below nonlinear truncation error. The facade bounds allocations before building the field, and requires a conservative Gaussian input bandwidth. The recorded native benchmarks distinguish measured peak RSS from the conservative memory estimate.

The differentiable route carries an initial-condition JVP through nLPT, or supplied phase-space directions through PM, to continuous P0 Fourier modes and power. It supports directional derivatives at fixed cosmology and clocks. It does not provide cosmological growth derivatives, a reverse-mode adjoint, or exact-clipped-density shape derivatives. Those are separate implementation tasks; they should not be implied by the word “differentiable.”

The browser uses Wasm and Canvas2D/SVG as the portable capability tier, with an optional checked GPU observer described below. The worker keeps large calculations off the page thread; the resource envelope permits lattice 64³ and observation/force grids up to 128³ when their combined estimate fits 1 GiB, while 1D and 2D ceilings are 1024 and 256². Invalid requests return explicit errors without replacing the requested grid. The same low-level Rust library supports caller-managed larger allocations outside the facade. The facade intentionally uses the same limits in native and Wasm runs so one manifest denotes one experiment.

## Data lineage and adaptation

The archival replay consists of extracted summary arrays, not entire simulation snapshots. Its manifest records repository, revision, source paths, checksums, and the extraction recipe. To substitute another dataset, preserve the estimator, filter, normalization, weighting, epoch, and crossing metadata. The original archival PDF histograms are conditional on their finite display range and do not report retained tail probabilities; the live PDF histograms preserve those probabilities separately. A new curve without those conventions cannot support a quantitative comparison.

To add a new observable, first derive its measure and normalization, test an analytic or independent reference, expose it through the Wasm facade, then add a URL state and a labeled plot. To change the gravitational model, keep the sheet's mass bookkeeping independent from the trajectory generator. This separation makes the continuous-sheet estimator useful for other forward models without treating a different trajectory as an LPT result.


## Reusing the cosmology and diagnostic policies

The physical initial-spectrum module is independent of the trajectory and geometric modules. `cosmological::gaussian_hat` returns grid FFT coefficients with an explicit physical box, $\sigma_8$ normalization, initial Gaussian filter, integer cutoff and early-normalized growth conversion. It keys Gaussian draws by integer mode so refinement preserves the same realization. A project can instead supply a verified tabulated spectrum while retaining the same mode-pairing and sheet measurement conventions.

`nbody::evolve_cosmology` accepts a `Cosmology`, state, optional tangent direction and an orientation policy. With `allow_crossing=true`, it records the first crossed drift bracket and continues the discrete evolution; with `false`, it returns an error. The strict `evolve_eds` wrapper preserves the original pre-crossing API. The orientation policy is separate from gravity and observation: it controls validity reporting, not the mass sign or force. All parameter derivatives currently hold cosmology and clocks fixed.

The checked `laboratory::run_json` facade accepts exported manifests as well as plain requests. Its `request` field is the executed numerical specification, independent of camera angle and selected panel. The appendix's lower-level examples deliberately expose more responsibility: callers must enforce conservative input bandwidth, compatible meshes, finite geometry and measured conservation themselves. Reuse of an exact overlap routine establishes exact integration of a supplied affine element; it does not certify the supplied trajectories.

## Hybrid WebGPU observation backend {#sec-gpu-backend}

The optional compute backend evaluates the continuous fixed-mass sheet modes and their analytic position directions. Rust/Wasm still constructs the initial field, integrates growth, builds nLPT and PM trajectories, checks orientation, clips the sheet onto the observation grid, and computes PDFs and gridded spectra. The backend changes the arithmetic used for selected continuous modes; it does not change the represented sheet, physical epoch, or estimator.

The prepared-run boundary retains the double-precision trajectory and tangent arrays. A GPU failure therefore reuses the prepared CPU state rather than repeating the physical calculation. Finalization uses the same Rust power normalization and unit conversion as the synchronous facade. The boundary is exposed by {{< src laboratory::prepare >}} and {{< src laboratory::PreparedLabRun >}}, and its compatibility and selective-recovery contracts are pinned by {{< test prepared_run_finishes_identically_and_validates_direct_channels "prepared-run contract" >}}.

| Stage | Arithmetic and execution |
|---|---|
| Initial conditions, growth and trajectory generation | Existing Rust/Wasm implementation |
| Exact density, PDFs and gridded power | Existing Rust/Wasm implementation |
| Continuous LPT/PM modes and analytic JVPs | Optional WGSL f32 kernel; CPU reference remains available |
| Weak LPT mode recovery | Retained CPU f64 trajectory and direction |
| Centered finite difference | CPU f64, value-only integral, cached per prepared run |
| Power, derivative and physical units | Rust f64 finalization |

For a fixed-mass simplex, the kernel evaluates the barycentric exponential divided difference and its repeated-knot derivative from @eq-simplex-fourier and @eq-amplitude-jvp. It retains periodic lifts and the same two-triangle or six-tetrahedron connectivity. The port adapts the stable local Taylor/Newton strategy from the MIT-licensed [Hopf–Cole direct kernel](https://github.com/yipihey/hopf-cole-cosmology/blob/3a3a13b9ba817c5b4f8f9f26314715845e13d4ad/app/js/gpu/direct.js). The [reuse manifest](../app/js/gpu/reuse-manifest.json) records original paths and hashes. Contributions are accumulated with an explicit reduction order and numerical diagnostics; no magnitude guard silently removes an element.

Displacements $\boldsymbol\psi=\boldsymbol x-\boldsymbol q$ are extracted in CPU f64 before conversion into packed f32 arrays. Integer lattice coordinates reconstruct the undeformed geometry. Only the exponential phase is reduced modulo $2\pi$; phase gaps in divided-difference denominators retain their full values. This distinction is necessary for both the primal integral and signed tangent coefficients. The four displacement/direction arrays occupy 16 MiB at $64^3$, before partial sums, staging and the retained CPU state.

The first backend covers 2D and 3D, including supported non-power-of-two lattices. One-dimensional requests use the CPU route. GPU resource refusal never changes the requested lattice, force mesh, observation mesh, bandwidth or epoch. A persistent numerical worker serializes requests, yields between bounded GPU submissions, discards obsolete generations, and releases owned buffers. During synchronous Rust preparation or CPU mode work, cancellation recreates the worker; during asynchronous GPU work it waits for submitted work and acknowledges cleanup.

### Precision, validation and reproduction

The portable [WGSL floating-point contract](https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#floating-point-types) supplies f32 rather than an f64 path. The [GPU self-check](../app/gpu-test.html) compares primal and JVP components with independently converged barycentric quadrature. The complete-request harness separately compares full-f64 Rust inputs, f64 kernels on quantized inputs, and GPU arithmetic. Its comparison target is $|\Delta F|\le10^{-6}+10^{-4}|F_{\rm ref}|$ component by component, with the same target for the JVP. This absolute floor makes cancellation-dominated modes interpretable; it does not assert uniform relative accuracy for arbitrarily weak modes.

The existing amplitude derivative gate remains a relative discrepancy of at most $10^{-5}$ against the CPU centered finite difference at $h=10^{-4}$. Separately reduced GPU f32 powers at $A\pm h$ are therefore not used for that check. When an LPT mode exceeds the gate, its value and tangent are recovered together on CPU f64; PM channels and passing LPT modes can remain on GPU. The manifest records the executed backend of each mode. This recovery is a numerical precision policy, independent of the shell-crossing caution.

CPU is the default. Selecting GPU attempts the accelerated observer and reports resource, capability or numerical fallback. Automatic selection remains on CPU until a device/workload policy is supported by accuracy and end-to-end measurements. Rendering uses the existing Canvas2D/SVG tier independently. Device limits, adapter metadata when exposed, shader hashes, reduction layout, stage durations and recovery decisions accompany the numerical results. Cross-device GPU replay uses stated tolerances rather than bitwise equality.

Run the independent kernel, complete cosmological requests, worker failure checks and repeated browser timings with:

```sh
make test
make test-wasm
node scripts/test_gpu.mjs --require-gpu --full --output gpu-checks.json
node scripts/test_gpu.mjs --require-gpu --benchmark --output gpu-benchmark.json
python3 scripts/profile_native_stages.py --dim 3 --repeats 3 --output native-profile.json
```

The browser runner requires Chrome (or `CHROME_PATH`) and has no npm dependencies. A missing adapter is reported as a skip; `--require-gpu` makes that a failing requirement. Normal hosted CI runs the native, Wasm and worker contracts, while GPU checks require a GPU-capable runner. See the [implementation plan](https://github.com/yipihey/precrossedsheet/blob/main/docs/webgpu-backend-plan.md) and [measurement record](https://github.com/yipihey/precrossedsheet/blob/main/docs/webgpu-results.md) for the tested requests and device-specific limits.

FFT/LPT residency, a GPU cosmological PM/KDK tangent solver and geometric clipping are subsequent stages. Hopf–Cole provides FFT and LPT foundations; its heat-flow model does not replace this laboratory's gravitational evolution. Extend a resident solver only after profiling the released hybrid path and passing independent trajectory, force, tangent and geometric tests.
